instructions: Grate the cucumber on the large holes of a box grater, using half of it. Squeeze it hard in a clean towel to get the water out. That should be about 1/2 cup.
In a bowl, stir together the squeezed cucumber, the yogurt, 1 minced garlic clove, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and 1/4 tsp salt. Put it in the fridge.
Grate the onion and 2 of the tomatoes on the large holes of the grater into a large bowl, with all their juices. Throw away the tomato skins.

Add the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 cup chopped parsley, 2 minced garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Mix with your hands until it just comes together. It will be soft and wet.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 8 patties, about 3 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the olive oil, then 4 of the patties. Cook for 3 minutes without moving them, until deep brown and they lift off the pan. Flip and cook for 3 minutes. You're cooking them to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest patty: it's done when it's no longer pink. Transfer to a plate.
Wipe out the pan, add 1 tbsp olive oil, and cook the other 4 patties the same way.

Meanwhile, cut the 2 remaining tomatoes into wedges and slice the rest of the cucumber into half moons. Put them in a bowl with 2 tbsp olive oil, the juice of half the lemon, the remaining 1/2 tsp oregano and 1/4 tsp salt. Crumble the feta over the top.
Cut the other half of the lemon into wedges.
Taste the salad. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve the patties with the tzatziki, the salad and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Honest time is about 34 minutes, a little over the 30 for a quick dinner, because the onion and tomatoes are grated and 8 patties are fried in two batches. The two versions read both bake the patties on lemon potatoes; this one pan-fries them as the dish was asked, and drops the potatoes. Both agree on grated onion and tomato in the mix, an egg and breadcrumbs for binding, and parsley; the second adds mint, cumin and cinnamon, which are left out here to keep it mild. The tzatziki is a plain yogurt, cucumber and garlic one, as neither source gave amounts.
